correctness.rationale: Proof uses an exact quadratic norm-character sum bounding primitive points on every affine Fp-line not through zero, then shows every length p−1 primitive progression must be the punctured line b Fp*. Cyclic exponent arithmetic yields the iff p−1 power-of-two criterion and exactly phi(p²−1) starts/steps. A p-term progression necessarily contains zero or more than (p+1)/2 points on a non-origin line, and primitive implies normal in degree two. Exact direct exhaustive tests at p=5,7,11,17 agree, without treating finite tests as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies and counts the longest possible nonrepeating primitive-normal progressions for every quadratic prime-field extension, giving a sharp arithmetic equivalence with Fermat primes. This is an all-characteristics additive/multiplicative rigidity theorem for a natural extremal variable m=p−1, rather than a single small-field calculation or reparametrization of a fixed-length sieve bound. The character-sum obstruction and scalar-coset dichotomy explain the boundary and provide a benchmark for higher extension degree.
